items.name: app-brand
items.title: App Brand
items.description: A compact TanStack Router brand link with a semantic icon, app name, and subtitle.
items.docs:
## Overview

`app-brand` provides a small reusable brand link for app shells, home page headers, and navigation chrome. It keeps the icon container, label, and subtitle visually consistent across pages. Use `to` for TanStack Router links, `href` for standard anchors, and `to={null}` for static branding. Internal links accept the same typed route props as TanStack Router's `Link`, including `params` and `search`.

## Usage

```tsx
import { AppBrand } from "@/components/ui/app-brand";
import { Blocks } from "lucide-react";

<AppBrand label="Krakstack" subtitle="Documentation" icon={Blocks} />
```

## Route Params

```tsx
<AppBrand
  to="/organizations/$organizationId"
  params={{ organizationId }}
  label="Acme"
  subtitle="Organization"
  icon={Blocks}
/>
```

items.name: copy-button
items.title: Copy Button
items.description: An accessible clipboard copy button with success and failure announcements for screen readers.
items.docs:
## Overview

`CopyButton` copies a string to the clipboard and announces copy results with an `aria-live` status region. It keeps the accessible name stable while the icon changes after a successful copy. Pass `valueDescription` for concise context, such as `install command` or `tsx code`; avoid passing the full copied value when it may be long or sensitive.

## Variants

- Omit `copyVariant` for the default icon-only size.
- `copyVariant="sm"` renders a smaller compact icon-only button.
- `copyVariant="large"` renders the copy label next to the icon.

## Usage

```tsx
import { CopyButton } from "@/components/ui/copy-button";

<CopyButton
  value="bun run dev"
  valueDescription="install command"
  copyVariant="large"
  variant="secondary"
  messages={{ copy: "Copy", copied: "Copied" }}
/>
```

## Overview

`Loading` renders a small spinner next to localized loading text. Use it inside pending pages, empty table states, cards, and inline loading regions. It defaults to the inline variant. Pass `variant="centered"` for route-level pending states and `label` to override the built-in English and French default.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Loading } from "@/components/ui/loading";

<Loading />
<Loading variant="centered" />
<Loading label="Refreshing records..." />
```

items.name: google-map
items.title: Google Map
items.description: A reusable Google Maps renderer with centered markers, radius circles, interaction controls, shared script loading, and localized states.
items.docs:
## Overview

`GoogleMap` is a product-neutral renderer for the Google Maps JavaScript API. The caller owns the browser API key and controlled map values; the component owns safe shared script loading, map initialization, centered overlays, status presentation, and cleanup. English and French status and accessibility labels are built in through `getLocale` and can be overridden with `messages`.

## Features

- Shared Google Maps script loading across component instances
- SSR-safe loading, missing-key, script failure, and initialization failure states
- Controlled center and zoom updates without recreating the map
- Optional centered marker with a custom icon URL
- Optional centered radius circle with fill and stroke customization
- Configurable interaction, zoom controls, and minimum and maximum zoom
- Semantic shadcn/Tailwind styling and localized accessibility labels

## API Key Requirement

Pass a browser key with the Google Maps JavaScript API enabled. Restrict the key to the consumer application's allowed HTTP referrers and do not pass a server key or secret. The component does not read environment variables or runtime configuration.

## Usage

```tsx
import { GoogleMap } from "@/components/ui/google-map";

<GoogleMap
  apiKey={googleMapsBrowserApiKey}
  center={{ lat: 45.5019, lng: -73.5674 }}
  zoom={11}
  className="h-96"
  marker
/>
```

`center` is a `{ lat, lng }` literal and `zoom` is clamped to `minZoom` and `maxZoom`. Provide a height through `className`; the default minimum height is `16rem`.

## Marker And Radius Customization

A boolean `marker` uses Google's default marker. Pass an object to supply an icon URL. `radiusMeters` is expressed in meters, and the circle always follows `center`.

```tsx
<GoogleMap
  apiKey={googleMapsBrowserApiKey}
  center={position}
  zoom={9}
  marker={{ icon: "/map-marker.svg" }}
  radius={{
    radiusMeters: 25_000,
    fillColor: "#2563eb",
    fillOpacity: 0.12,
    strokeColor: "#1d4ed8",
    strokeOpacity: 0.8,
    strokeWeight: 2,
  }}
/>
```

## Interaction Constraints

Set `interactive={false}` for a static preview. This disables dragging, gestures, scrolling, keyboard shortcuts, and clickable map icons while leaving the optional custom zoom controls available. Set `zoomControls={false}` to hide the component's plus/minus controls independently of direct map interaction. `minZoom` and `maxZoom` constrain both prop updates and custom controls. All map instances on a page share one Google Maps script and should receive the same API key. Remount the component to retry after a script-load failure. Google Maps usage remains subject to Google's API availability, billing, and terms.

items.name: form
items.title: Form
items.description: A TanStack Form setup with reusable field wrappers, compact and searchable selects, file inputs, submit state, and dirty-navigation blocking.
items.docs:
## Overview

`form` creates an application form hook with reusable field components for common admin and product workflows. It standardizes labels, descriptions, validation messages, submit state, file inputs, image inputs, and dirty-navigation protection. Built-in labels are stored in the component file and can be overridden with message props on the relevant field or form component.

## Features

- Typed `useAppForm` hook built on TanStack Form
- Text, textarea, select, multi-select, checkbox, file, image, and key/value fields
- Field wrappers for grouped form sections
- Submit button wired to form submission state
- Dirty-navigation confirmation through TanStack Router
- In-file English and French defaults with override props

## Usage

```tsx
const form = useAppForm({
  defaultValues: { name: "Ada" },
  onSubmit: async ({ value }) => save(value),
});

<form.AppForm>
  <form.AppField name="name">
    {(field) => <field.TextField label="Name" />}
  </form.AppField>
  <form.SubmitButton messages={{ submit: "Save" }} />
</form.AppForm>
```

## File Selection Side Effects

`FileField` accepts `onFileChange` when selecting a file needs to update adjacent UI, upload metadata, or derived form state before submit.

```tsx
<form.AppField name="attachment">
  {(field) => (
    <field.FileField
      accept=".pdf,.txt"
      label="Attachment"
      onFileChange={(file) => setSelectedFile(file || null)}
    />
  )}
</form.AppField>
```

items.name: effect-form
items.title: Effect Form
items.description: Reusable Effect Form fields, submission state, errors, grouping, file inputs, and dirty-navigation blocking.
items.docs:
## Overview

`effect-form` provides reusable field components for `@lucas-barake/effect-form-react`. It includes schema-backed fields, submission errors and state, grouped fields, revert actions, and form-owned dirty-navigation blocking. Built-in English and French labels can be read or overridden with `effectFormMessages`.

## Available Fields

- `TextField` and `NameField` — string inputs, with a standard localized name variant
- `TextAreaField`, `DescriptionField`, and `NullableTextAreaField` — required and nullable multiline values
- `CheckboxField` — boolean values
- `SelectField` and `FolderField` — single string selection
- `MultiSelectField` and `NullableMultiSelectField` — array and nullable array selection
- `SearchableSelectField` and `SingleSearchableSelectField` — virtualized searchable multiple and single selection
- `KeyValueField` and `NullableKeyValueField` — record editors
- `FileField` — clearable native `File` values through the shared `FilePicker`
- `ImageField` — local file and persisted URL image values with previews
- `RevertButton` — restores a string field to its original value

## Form Helpers

- `FieldWrapper` groups related fields with a legend and optional locale badge
- `SubmitButton` observes dirty, changed-since-submit, and waiting state
- `SubmitError` and `ErrorMessage` present typed failures
- `BlockNavigation` observes the form and guards unsaved navigation

## Usage

```tsx
const builder = FormBuilder.empty.addField("name", Schema.String);

const form = FormReact.make(builder, {
  fields: { name: TextField },
  onSubmit: (_, { decoded }) => save(decoded),
});

<form.Initialize defaultValues={{ name: "" }}>
  <form.name label="Name" />
  <SubmitError result={submitResult} />
  <SubmitButton form={form} />
  <BlockNavigation form={form} />
</form.Initialize>
```

## Overview

`locale-switcher` provides a compact language switcher for Paraglide projects. It reads the current locale from Paraglide, lists the configured locales, and updates the active locale from a dropdown menu.

## Features

- Uses Paraglide `getLocale`, `setLocale`, and `locales`
- In-file English and French labels
- Optional message overrides
- Icon-only trigger with accessible screen-reader text

## Usage

```tsx
import { LocaleSwitcher } from "@/components/ui/locale-switcher";

<LocaleSwitcher />

<LocaleSwitcher messages={{ title: "Language", en: "EN", fr: "FR" }} />
```

items.title: Editing Locale Switcher
items.description: A compact localized select for choosing which locale is being edited in multilingual forms.
items.docs:
## Overview

`editing-locale-switcher` provides a small form control for switching the active editing locale in multilingual forms. It is useful for forms that store localized fields in metadata or translation maps.

## Features

- Typed `EditingLocale` union for English and French
- Controlled `value` and `onValueChange` props
- Mobile-friendly icon label with desktop text
- In-file English and French labels with optional message overrides

## Usage

```tsx
import { EditingLocaleSwitcher, type EditingLocale } from "@/components/ui/editing-locale-switcher";
import { useState } from "react";

const [locale, setLocale] = useState<EditingLocale>("en");

<EditingLocaleSwitcher value={locale} onValueChange={setLocale} />
<EditingLocaleSwitcher value={locale} onValueChange={setLocale} messages={{ label: "Language" }} />
```

items.name: service-notification
items.title: Notification Service
items.description: A legacy source-vendored direct Effect dispatcher retained for compatibility; durable systems should use @krak-stack/notifications.
items.docs:
## Compatibility Status

`service-notification` is the source-vendored direct compatibility dispatcher. It sends top-level channel messages through an application-composed `NotificationChannelRegistry` and remains available for projects that already own this source. It is not the recommended durable notification system.

New applications that need package-owned migrations, inbox and preference CRUD, delivery attempts, Effect persisted-queue jobs, retries, a scheduler, workers, or one-shot reminders should install `@krak-stack/notifications`.

## Included Files

- `services/notification/index.ts` - Direct `NotificationService`, optional persistence-store contract, and layer helpers
- `services/notification/channels/index.ts` - Compatibility channel contract and registry
- `services/notification/schema.ts` - Dynamic message envelope and shared send error

## Direct Dispatch

```ts
const notifications = yield* NotificationService;

yield* notifications.send({
  email: {
    to: "user@example.com",
    subject: "Password reset",
    text: "Use the secure link to reset your password.",
  },
});
```

Install `notification-channel-email-ses` when this compatibility dispatcher should send through SES. For the durable package, import the provider adapter from `@krak-stack/notifications/transport/email-ses` or `/transport/email-smtp` instead.

## Optional Store Hook

The structured `{ persist, message }` form can call a consumer-provided `NotificationPersistenceStore` before optional direct channel dispatch. The application still owns that store, its transaction boundary, authorization, migrations, relay, retry policy, and workers. Adding the hook does not turn this compatibility item into the durable `@krak-stack/notifications` runtime.

items.name: notification-persistence
items.title: Notification Persistence
items.description: A legacy source-install option for app-owned PostgreSQL notification tables and codecs; new apps should use @krak-stack/notifications.
items.docs:
## Legacy Source-Install Option

`notification-persistence` vendors three project-owned PostgreSQL tables into an application: `notifications`, `notification_settings`, and `notification_deliveries`. It also vendors Effect record schemas and versioned payload codecs. It remains available for projects that intentionally own their Drizzle schema and worker implementation.

New durable notification systems should install `@krak-stack/notifications` instead. The package owns migrations, inbox CRUD, preference and suppression CRUD, delivery attempts and references, Effect persisted-queue jobs, the scheduler and workers, and one-shot reminders.

## Included Files

- `services/notification/persistence/drizzle.ts` - Legacy Drizzle tables, indexes, constraints, and inferred row types
- `services/notification/persistence/schema.ts` - Legacy record schemas, lifecycle values, and payload codecs
- `services/notification/persistence/index.ts` - Server-only compatibility exports

## Existing Applications

Re-export the installed definitions from the app's Drizzle schema only while the application remains the migration owner:

```ts
export * from "@/services/notification/persistence/drizzle";
```

This item provides no authorization queries, CRUD service, migrations, relay, scheduler, retry runtime, or worker. The application must implement and operate all of those concerns.

## Adopt `@krak-stack/notifications`

Preserve the three existing tables and stop every application-owned relay and worker before cutover. The package's additive migration adopts their data, reconciles legacy `processing` rows, and imports disabled rows from a compatible `email_preferences` table. Move application correlations to `notification_delivery_references`, then exclude all package-owned notification and queue tables from application Drizzle migrations. See the Notifications guide for the complete cutover sequence.

items.name: seo
items.title: SEO Metadata
items.description: A framework-neutral SEO helper for TanStack Start head metadata, localized canonical links, Open Graph and Twitter tags, and derived JSON-LD.
items.docs:
## Overview

`createSeo` creates a configured SEO helper for public pages. Put site-wide values such as the origin, supported locales, site name, and organization profiles in the factory, then pass only page-specific metadata to each page. The lower-level `seo` function remains available for one-off configurations.

## Install

```bash
bunx shadcn@latest add @krak-stack/seo
```

The item installs `src/lib/seo.ts`. The same helper is available from the package export `@krak-stack/registry/seo`.

## Configure Site Defaults

```tsx
import { createSeo } from "@/lib/seo";

const siteSeo = createSeo({
  origin: "https://example.com",
  locales: ["en", "fr"],
  siteName: "Example",
  sameAs: ["https://github.com/example/project"],
});
```

## Page Metadata

Use the configured helper in a TanStack Start route. `path` defaults to `/`, and `defaultLocale` falls back to the first configured locale.

```tsx
export const Route = createFileRoute("/")({
  head: () =>
    siteSeo({
      title: "Example",
      description: "Production-ready building blocks for TanStack apps.",
      locale: "en",
      image: "https://example.com/og.png",
    }),
});
```

The returned `meta`, `links`, and `scripts` can be spread into a route head configuration. Optional values are omitted instead of producing empty tags.

## Documentation Pages

Pass `type: "article"` and a page path for documentation or other editorial pages. This changes the JSON-LD payload from `WebSite` to `Article`.

```tsx
siteSeo({
  title: "Introduction",
  description: "Learn the core concepts.",
  path: "/docs/introduction",
  locale: "en",
  type: "article",
});
```

## Factory Options

- `origin` - site origin used to derive canonical and localized URLs
- `locales` - supported locales used for alternate links
- `defaultLocale` - locale used for the `x-default` link
- `siteName` - site and publisher name
- `twitterCreator` and `twitterSite` - Twitter profile handles
- `sameAs` - organization profile URLs included in JSON-LD

## Page Options

- `title` - required page title
- `description` - description used by search and social metadata
- `path` - page path, defaulting to `/`
- `locale` - current page locale
- `url` - explicit canonical URL when it cannot be derived
- `image` - social preview image URL
- `robots` - custom robots directive, defaulting to `index, follow`
- `type` - `website` or `article`, defaulting to `website`

items.name: agents
items.title: AGENTS.md
items.description: Project configuration and coding guidelines for AI agents, covering i18n, service patterns, Effect schemas, HTTP API groups, optimistic atoms, and lint/typecheck commands.
items.docs:
## Overview

`agents` installs the `AGENTS.md` file that guides AI agents working in a KrakStack project. It covers i18n conventions, code architecture, Effect service patterns, schema and API documentation rules, and the commands used to validate changes.

## Sections

- **i18n** — Paraglide.js conventions, message file ownership, and English/French requirements
- **Code Architecture** — Frontend (TanStack Start, shadcn, Effect atoms) and backend (Effect SQL, PostgreSQL) structure
- **Patterns** — Server services, frontend client components, SQL schemas and migrations, API composition, schema annotations, and documentation rules
- **Examples** — Effect schema, API group, API builder, form dialog, data table, optimistic atom, Effect SQL service, migrations, and API entry point code
- **Preferences** — Arrow functions, no type assertions
- **Checks** — `bun type:check`, `bun lint`, `bun fmt`

## Usage

Place `AGENTS.md` at the project root so agent tooling can read it automatically:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add https://krakstack.net/r/agents.json
```

After installation, open `AGENTS.md` and adjust the folder structure, patterns, and check commands to match your project.

items.name: lint-format
items.title: Lint & Format Config
items.description: Production-ready Oxfmt and Oxlint configuration for KrakStack projects, including vendored anti-slop rules, Tailwind class sorting, and React/TypeScript correctness checks.
items.docs:
## Overview

`lint-format` installs root-level Oxfmt and Oxlint configuration for KrakStack projects. It includes editable source for KrakStack's Oxlint plugin, initially based on anti-slop's opinionated rules for rejecting low-evidence TypeScript and JavaScript patterns. The plugin is vendored so each project can inspect, customize, and extend its rules.

## Included Files

- `.oxfmtrc.json` — Oxfmt config with 80-column formatting and Tailwind CSS class sorting
- `.oxlintrc.json` — Oxlint config for React, TypeScript, browser, Node, and the vendored plugin
- `tools/oxlint/anti-slop/` — editable Oxlint plugin source and shared rule utilities

## Choices

- Vendors plugin source instead of coupling projects to a fixed lint package release
- Enables all anti-slop rules as errors
- Ignores installed agent tooling and the plugin source itself
- Uses JSON config files so CLI tooling can load them reliably across Node and Bun runtimes
- Enables `sortTailwindcss` for shadcn/Tailwind projects
- Disables `eslint/require-yield` because Effect uses generator functions as a DSL
- Enables Vitest globals only in test files

## Usage

Install the registry item:

```bash
bunx shadcn@latest add @krak-stack/lint-format
```

Recommended package scripts:

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "lint": "oxlint",
    "fmt": "oxfmt",
    "fmt:check": "oxfmt --check ."
  }
}
```

Run checks locally or in CI:

```bash
bun run fmt:check
bun run lint
```

items.title: Virtualized Combobox
items.description: A searchable, virtualized Base UI combobox with single and multiple selection, controlled search, custom triggers, and localized labels.
items.docs:
## Overview

`VirtualizedCombobox` combines Base UI and TanStack Virtual into a complete searchable selector for large or remotely filtered option sets. It supports single and multiple selection, controlled open and search state, custom item rendering, and custom triggers.

## Usage

```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState(null);

<VirtualizedCombobox
  ariaLabel="Select a city"
  emptyLabel="No cities found."
  items={cities}
  onValueChange={setValue}
  placeholder="Select a city"
  value={value}
/>
```

Set `multiple` and pass an array value for multi-selection. Use `searchValue` and `onSearchValueChange` for remote search.
